parsed.stack: React Native (both siblings' phones matter equally), plus a plain web view. On-device ASR for the 30-second dictation, then a Haiku-class pass to structure it (who, what, amount, date). Q&A holds the household's whole record in a long context window with prompt caching (~90% off cached input) - no vector DB. Postgres on Supabase for the shared thread, per-household invite links, role-based read access. Freemium subscription, App Store + Play Store.
milestones: Week 1-2: 30-second dictate-after-a-call capture with on-device ASR, structured into a dated entry with zero typing.
Week 3-4: the shared thread and the invite-for-function loop - the second sibling must get value in the first 60 seconds without any setup.
Week 5-6: ask-the-log over the full household history with caching, answering 'what did the furnace guy say in March and who paid him' with citations back to the specific entry.
Week 7: receipts and appointment attachments, contractor contact extraction, export for the sibling who does the taxes.
Week 8-9: freemium gate (2 people and 3 months of history free, paid for more), pilot with 15 sibling pairs found through carer forums.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That 30-second dictations from two or three siblings accumulate into a record with enough factual anchors - names, dates, amounts - that the long-context answer is correct rather than a confident reconstruction; a thin log makes the no-retrieval-pipeline pitch vacuous and a wrong answer about who paid the furnace guy is worse than no answer.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Take one family's real six months of texts and call notes, paste them into a long context window as-is, and ask twenty questions a sibling would actually ask - measure how many are answered correctly with a citation versus plausibly confabulated.
